full_judgment:
AKM Shahidul Huq J: The proceedings of Motijheel PS Case No. 86 dated 19-7-2007 under sections 385/109/206 of the Penal Code corresponding to GR No. 746 of 2007 pending in the 5th Court of Joint Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka has been called in question by invoking the inherent jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court as laid down in section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in which a Division Bench of this Hon'ble Court on perusal of the application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and on hearing the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners was pleased to issue a Rule calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the criminal proceeding of Motijheel PS Case No. 86 dated 19-7-2007 under sections 385/109/506 of the Penal Code corresponding to GR No. 746/2007 pending in the 5th Joint Metropolitan Session Judge Court, Dhaka vide Session Case No. 9875 of 2011 should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The accused-petitioners seek to quash the criminal proceeding of Motijheel PS Case No. 86 dated 19-7-2007 under sections 385/109/506 of the Penal Code corresponding to GR No. 746/2007, now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka mainly on the grounds that the facts of the instant case are so preposterous and absurd that upon which no criminal case can be continued and the informant in a malafide motive lodged the instant case with a view to harass, humiliate the accused-petitioners as the petitioners are the legal Counsel of Taehung Packaging BD Ltd. a Private Ltd. Company owned by the accused No. 4 conducted all the cases lodged by the present informant and, as such, the entire proceedings being malafide and the abuse of the process of the Court is liable to be quashed to secure the ends of justice. 

 3. During the State of Emergency while the accused-petitioners were in jail custody in connection with some false and frivolous cases lodged by different interested persons at the instance of the then Caretaker Government, the informant being highly influenced by the then Law Advisor lodged a First Information Report with Motijheel Police Station being Motijheel PS Case No. 86 dated 19-7-2007 under sections 385/109/506 of the Penal Code against the accused-petitioner and others alleging inter alia, that the informant was the Managing Director of Taehung Pacaking (BD) Ltd. and owner of shares valued about US $ 370,000. The accused No. 4 was the Chairman of the said company who with the help of some corrupt persons in Bangladesh was making all sorts of attempts to misappropriate the shares of the informant lying with the said company. In the year 2004, the accused No. 4 created a false resignation letter by forging the signature of the informant and submitted it to the Registrar of Joint-Stock Companies and Firms. There was hot talk with Mr Monir Hossain Kazol at the office of the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firm at Motijheel and at that point of time Mr Ashanur Rahman, sent some police personnel for arresting the informant but could not succeed in arresting her due to the presence of some journalists which was reported in the daily Newspaper namely "Amar Desh" on the following day. The accused persons in many ways harassed the informant in forcefully ousting her from the company and getting arrested and putting her in jail by using police, filing false cases by misusing the powers. On various occasions the accused persons threatened her with dire consequences including her death if she filed any complaint. Hence, the informant lodged aforesaid FIR against the accused-petitioners and others. 

 4. The case was taken up by the police for investigation and on conclusion of the investigation submitted a charge-sheet against all the FIR named accused persons excepting the accused No. 3 whose mobile was allegedly used by the accused No. 2 to commit the offence as alleged in the FIR. 

 5. Mr Ashanur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that where the allegations made in the First Information Report and other materials if any, accompanying do not disclose any offence and the allegation made in the FIR are so absurd and preposterous and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can never reach to a just conclusion that there are sufficient grounds for proceeding against the accused and where the proceeding is manifestly attended with malafide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vigilance on the accused with a view to spite them due to private and personal grudge. The allegations as alleged being inherently improbable, absurd and preposterous and the case being a very rare case is liable to be interfered with by the Hon'ble High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 6. He submits that where the facts of the case are so preposterous and the FIR and other material disclose no offence, the provision of section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is very much attracted. 

 7. Learned Advocate also submits that the case is tainted by inordinate delay of more than 2 years and the explanation as given in the FIR is not satisfactory. 

 9. The learned Advocate for the petitioners in support of his contention refers an unreported case of Tae Hung packaging (BD) Limited Bangladesh passed in Writ Petition No. 10675 of 2007 Nazmul Huda Bangladesh in Writ Petition No. 719 of 2008 vs. Bangladesh represented by the Secretary Ministry of Home Affairs also refers the case of Abdul Kader Chowdhury vs State reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38 relevant para 11. The case of M/s Khawza vs State reported in 17 DLR (SC) 153, relevant para 4 and 5. The case of Md Shamsuddin @ Lambo vs State reported in 40 DLR (AD) 69 relevant para 3. The case of Akhter Rahman vs State and Sultan Ahmed reported in 35 DLR High Court Division page in Criminal Revision No. 484 of 1981 relevant para 5 and lastly refers the case of The State of Urisha vs Gonesh Chandra Jhew reported in AIR SC 2004 page 2179 relevant para 21. He next refers the case of M/s Pepsi Foods Ltd. vs Special Magistrate reported in AIR SC 1998 page 128. 

 12. Before entering into the merit of the case, let us first see the provision of law as contain in section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 13. Now let us see the decisions of our Apex Court in this regard. It is held in the case of Bangladesh vs Shahjahan Seraj reported in 32 DLR (SC) Page 1. 

 14. Our Supreme Court held in the case of Abdul Kader Chowdhury vs State reported in 28 DLR (SC) 38. 

 15. It is held in the case of Md Shamuddin @ Lambu vs State: 

 16. Our Appellate Division held in the case of Ali Akkas vs Enayet Hossain reported in 17 BLD (AD) 44 = 2 BLC (AD) 16. 

 "In a case where the allegations in FIR or the petition of complaint, even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirely do not constitute the offence alleged." 

 17. In the case of Abdul Kader Chowdhury vs State reported in 28 DLR (AD), where our Apex Court held that:- 

 "Ordinarily criminal proceedings instituted against an accused person must be tried under the provisions of the Code and the said proceedings should not be generally interfered with at an interlocutory stage in exercise of the inherent jurisdiction provided under section 561A of the Code. But a pertinent question may be posed as to when and under what circumstances the said jurisdiction can and should be exercised by the High Court Division. The consensus of judicial opinion is that it is not possible, desirable or expedient to lay down any inflexible rule which should govern the exercise of this inherent jurisdiction. The exercise of this jurisdiction will depend upon the facts and circumstances of each case. Interference even at an initial stage may be justified where the facts are so preposterous that even on the admitted facts no case can stand against the accused and that a further prolongation of the prosecution would amount to harassment to an innocent party and abuse of the process of the court." 

 18. In the case of Shamsuddin Lambo vs State reported in 40 DLR (AD), where our Apex Court held that:- 

 In all these cases though there was a delay of considerable time, the court refused to quash the proceeding because delay by itself is not a ground for quashing the criminal proceedings. But when a case is made out that the prosecution has been launched from an improper motive only to harass the accused due to personal vendetta whether the court should exercise such jurisdiction which has been given power to prevent the abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice It is needless to mention that the machinery of administration of justice should not be allowed to harass any innocent person." 

 19. In the case of Tae Hung Packaging (BD) Ltd. Bangladesh vs Bangladesh represented by the Secretary Ministry of Home Affairs reported in 31 DLR (AD) 69 where our Apex Court held that:- 

 "Section 561A emphasises that the High Court has the jurisdiction to pass orders to secure the ends of justice and for that purpose the High Court is competent to entertain applications not provided by the Code. However, it must be clearly understood that the terms of section 561A of the Code do not extend the jurisdiction of the High Court to matters which are not inherently with that jurisdiction. The High Court also cannot claim inherent jurisdiction to exercise powers taken away by legislation. When exercising this jurisdiction, the High Court would not embark upon an enquiry whether the evidence in question is reliable or not. This is the function of the trial Magistrate and it might so happen that quashment of a criminal proceeding before commencement of trial would amount to stifling the proceedings before the prosecution got an opportunity to bring evidence in support of the accusation. That is why their Lordships of the judicial Committee in the case of Emperor vs Nazir Ahmed expressed a word of caution that the court might be acting on treacherous grounds" in quashing of criminal proceedings at the interlocutory stage or at the early stage on the ground that continuation of the proceedings would be an abuse of the process of the court. We equally agree with the view taken by their Lordships of the Judicial Committee that the extraordinary power of the court under section 561A should be exercised very cautiously to avoid miscarriage of justice". 

 20. In the case of Akhter Rahman vs State reported in 35 DLR High Court Division page 100 where our Apex Court held that:- 

 22. In the case of Kazi Khairuzzaman vs State reported in 18 MLR 78 held that:- 

 23. Now let us see the decisions of our Apex Court held in the case of Bangladesh vs Shahjahan Seraj reported in 32 DLR (SC) 1: 

 24. Our Supreme Court held in the case of Abdul Kader Chowdhury vs State reported in 28 DLR (SC) 38. 

 25. It is held in the case of Md Shamsuddin & Lambu vs State. 

 26. Our Appellate Division held in the case of Ali Akkas vs Enayet Hossain reported in 17 BLD (AD) 44 = 2 BLC (AD) 16. 

 "In a case where the allegations in FIR or the petition of complaint, even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirely do not constitute the offence alleged." 

 "In a case where the allegations in FIR or the petition of complaint, even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not constitute the offence alleged". 

 27. The principle of law as regards the sheer abuse of the process of the Court as laid down in section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been well founded, explained and settled in a number of decisions of our Apex Court as well as High Court Division. Now let us analyze and see how the principle of law of the sheer abuse of the process of the court has been applied by our Apex Court as well as High Court Division in a number of cases. In the case of Shafiqul Alam vs. State reported in 65 DLR 83 where a Division Bench of this Hon'ble Court held that:- 

 "There is nothing in the FIR and charge sheet to show as to how the accused petitioner held connivance with the principal accused in the matter of creating forged document. The facts disclosed in the FIR and charge sheet do not attract any offence against the accused petitioner to proceed against him. Continuation of such proceeding after taking cognizance would be sheer abuse of process of the court. A criminal proceeding starts from the date of taking cognizance and if it is found that the allegation made in the FIR or prima facie case, against the accused petitioner. Continuation of such proceeding would be useless and preposterous and, as such, it is an abuse of the process of the court rendering the same liable to be quashed." 

 28. In the case of Rabeya Khanam vs State reported in Apex Law Reports 2013 page 5 in which one of us was a party where it was held that:- 

 "The accused petitioner is a retired professor of Botany of a government College who was 67 years aged. It was not disclosed in the FIR that under what capacity the informant lodged complaint against the accused petitioner before the administrator. This shows that informant is being used as a tool by some persons out of grudge and enmity. The allegations brought against the petitioner is so preposterous and absurd that cannot be believed for which the police also submitted the final report and, as such, the proceeding should be stopped in order to prevent the abuse of the process of the court. Since the intention of the proceeding is the product of falsehood and grudge and since no prima facie case against the petitioner has not been made out and facts as disclosed in the FIR are so preposterious that no proceeding can be taken against the petitioner. Hence the proceeding is quashed." 

 29. In the case of Md Obaidul Hoque Obaidullah Obaidul Islam @ Obaidullah reported in 20 BLT (HCD) 44 where a Division Bench of this Hon'ble Court held that:- 

 "In the instant case, if the allegations made in the FIR charge sheet, contents of statements of witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and other materials on record are taken together at its face value and accepted in its entirety which do not constitute any offence alleged against the petitioners. We find it is a fit case to interfere at this stage under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure to prevent the abuse of the process of the court and to secure the ends of justice and thus the continuation of such proceedings well be a flagrant abuse of the process of the court and such process of law must not be used as an engine of harassment. In the case of Mrs Taslima Khatoon vs State reported in 20 BLT (HCD) 90 where a Division Bench of this Hon'ble Court held that:- 

 "In the instant case, allegations against the two accused petitioners are that they have misappropriated certain amount of Government money that was allocated for the development purpose. In doing so they were able to obtain recommendation of the then MP for that constituency and also the then Speaker and ultimately received the money through the DC office, but they did not utilize the money so received. In view of such situation the former speaker was an accused in the FIR and also in the charge sheet. But the said principal accused the then Speaker has been withdrawn by the Government from the prosecution held the learned Special Judge has no jurisdiction to hold trial of the case by framing charge against the accused petitioners who are admittedly not public servants as per the prosecution documents. The learned Special Judge ion his order dated 25-9-2002 recorded the same finding that two accused petitioners are not public servants. So we hold that the proceedings of the case is before a court which is quorum nonjudice in view of section 5(a) read with item No. (b) of the Schedule to the Act 1958. So in our view the continuation of the proceeding in the court of the Special Judge being a court without jurisdiction would be an abuse of process." 

 30. In the case of Rafiqul Islam vs State reported in 20 BLC 334 where a Division Bench of this Hon'ble Court held that:- 

 "Initation of the criminal case at the insance of the complainant without taking recourse of the procedures specifically provided in the ordinance is not maintainable in law. Since initiation of the case is barred by law this court in exercise of its jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code can quash the proceeding at its initial stage before taking cognizance thereof". 

 In passing the judgment by the High Court Division the Division Bench of this Hon'ble Court relied upon the case of Abdul Kader Chowdhury vs State reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38, M. Farnsis P. Rojario @ Babu vs State reported in 62 DLR 355, KM Nurul Islam vs State reported in 14 BLC 514, Ali Akkas vs Enayet Hossain reported in 17 BLD (AD) 44, Sher Ali (Md) vs State reported in 46 DLR AD 67, 31 DLR (AD) 69, 36 DLR AD 14, 48 DLR AD 87, 61 DLR (AD) 93, 2007 BLD page 47. 

 31. In the case of MA Sukkur vs Md Zahirul Haque passed in Criminal Appeal No. 26 of 2005 reported in 23 BLT 2015 where our Apex Court held that "The allegations of bounding of cheque simpliciter does not ipso facts constitute an offence as defined under section 115 of the Penal Code punishable under section 420 of the Penal Code and, as such, framing of charge against the appellant under section 420 of the Penal Code suffered from serious illegality. Having gone through the petition of complaint it appears that there is no ingredient disclosing any criminal offence not to speak of any offence punishable under section 420 of the Penal Code. The normal financial transaction between debtor and creditor does not come within the scope of any offence. In view of the findings above we find substance in the appeal. 

 32. Accordingly this appeal is allowed and all further proceedings in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1876 of 1997 under section 420 of the Penal Code now pending in the court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate is quashed. 

 33. The scope of quashing the proceedings have been well explained in the case of Foyez Ahmed vs State reported in 37 BLD 570 in which a Division Bench of this Hon'ble Court relying the decision of Abdul Kader Chowdhury vs State spelt out the four criteria upon which the High Court Division normally interfere with the initiation of any proceeding in a criminal Court against any person. 

 (a) Interference even at an initial stage may be justified where the facts are so preposterous that even on the admitted facts no case can stand against the accused. 

 (c) Where there is a legal bar against institution or continuance of a criminal case against an accused person. 

 (d) In a case where the allegations in the First Information Report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not constitute the offence alleged and in such cases no question of weighing and appreciating evidence arises, and 

 (e) The allegations made against the accused person do constitute an offence alleged but there is either no legal evidence adduced in support of the case or the evidence adduced clearly or manifestly fails to prove the charge. 

 34. On careful consideration of the materials on record it appears that out of a well-planned design the petitioners have been falsely implicated in the case, it further appears that the facts of the case is so preposterous that no criminal case stands against the petitioners. The judicial process should not be allowed to be abuse in such a way out of vendetta and enmity for the sake of upholding the confidence of the peoples in our justice delivery system and, as such, it is reasonably presumed that the accused petitioners are the victims of a grave conspiracy and design, it appears that the accused petitioners are absolutely innocent and they never committed any offence as alleged against them and they have been falsely implicated in the case only for harassment and humiliation. 

 35. In the foregoing facts and circumstances and the submissions as advanced and the citations as referred by the learned Advocate in support of his contention and considering the material facts we find that no prima facie case against the accused petitioners have been established to connect the petitioners with the alleged commission of offence and we also find that the allegations have been falsely brought against the accused petitioners only to harass and humiliate. Considering the above facts and circumstances we find that it is a fit case to interfere at this stage under the provision of law as contain in section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure to prevent the abuse of the process of the court and to secure the ends of justice and thus the continuation of such proceeding will be a flagrant abuse of the process of the court and, as such, process of law must be not used as an engine of harassment. In view of the above facts and circumstances of the case we find that the instant proceeding against the accused petitioners are nothing but an abuse of the process of the court and interference of this court is required under the inherent jurisdiction to secure the ends of justice and the said proceeding is liable to be quashed. The citations as referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioners in support of his contentions are fully applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case. 

 36. Accordingly, the rule is made absolute. The criminal proceeding of Motijheel PS Case No. 86 dated 19-7-2007 under sections 385/109/506 of the Penal Code corresponding to GR No. 766 of 2007 now pending in the 5th Court of Joint Metropolitan Sessions Judge vide Sessions Case No. 9875 of 2011 is hereby quashed in respect of the petitioners only.
